clue.text: They include the following eight

parts.note: the figure printed straight after the clue, the count of eight, sits between a pair of round marks on the page

explanation.surface: Some group takes in the next eight people or things.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at its own letter count: the 8 printed after it is enclosed in the very punctuation marks the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentheses enclose text, and here they enclose the count figure that follows the clue.

clue.text: Popular opium, one said.

parts.note: Karl Marx called faith the opium of the people, so the drug of the populace, as one thinker said

explanation.surface: Someone once claimed a well-liked narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx wrote that faith is 'the opium of the people'; 'one' is Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx famously described faith and worship as the opiate of the masses.

clue.text: Politician in a jam — comes round at four

indicators.note: comes round says the jam word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: conserve is preserved fruit, jam
taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An MP in trouble comes to at four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a jam' suggests trouble; 'comes round' (recovers consciousness) puts CONSERVE around AT and IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory MP or party member is a politician of the right.

clue.text: Trade not for robbers.

parts.note: the proverb says a fair swap is no robbery, so this kind of trade is not the business of thieves

explanation.surface: A line of business that thieves avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: It leans on the saying 'a fair exchange is no robbery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading means swapping goods, one thing given for another.

clue.text: Leaves brewer in Moscow ?

parts.note: leaves are tea leaves, and a brewer of tea in Russia is the traditional heated urn

explanation.surface: A man who makes beer departs while in the Russian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian tea urn heats water for brewing tea.

clue.text: A tract, in general

definitions.meaning: a stretch of land open to the public

explanation.surface: Some land, broadly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Common land is a tract open to all, and general can mean shared by all or usual.

clue.text: Peer's follower in play?

parts.note: Peer is the first name of Ibsen's title character, so the word after it in the play's title

explanation.surface: A nobleman's attendant in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Peer is not a lord but Ibsen's hero in the play Peer Gynt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's verse drama is named after its hero, whose surname follows his first name.

clue.text: They wouldn't thank one for disclosing fuel locations

definitions.text: They wouldn't thank one for disclosing fuel locations

parts.words: They wouldn't thank one for disclosing fuel locations
parts.note: ungrateful people would show no thanks; split differently, the word says where coal sits in a fireplace

explanation.surface: Some people would not be grateful if you revealed where the fuel is.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN GRATES, where fuel is found in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungrateful people never thank anyone.

clue.text: It's the devil to get ahead over there!

parts.note: read as 'a head': POLL is an old word for the head, so a head gives A POLL
yon is an archaic word for that place yonder

explanation.surface: Getting on in life is a fiendishly hard thing to manage abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' must be split as 'a head'; POLL for head survives in 'poll tax', a tax per head.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon is the destroying angel of Revelation, a biblical name for Satan.

clue.text: Design for machinery not finished ?

indicators.note: not finished says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: plant means the machinery of a factory

explanation.surface: A blueprint for some apparatus is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts the last letter, T, from PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or layout, which is what a plan sets out.

clue.text: Fish together a rough stream, with an instructor

parts.note: a school is a group of fish swimming together

indicators.note: rough here means roughly handled, so the letters of the next word are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher goes fishing with others in a turbulent river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns STREAM into MASTER, joined after SCHOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher in a school, especially an old-fashioned male one, is an instructor of pupils.

clue.text: Lily King's ale's spilled

parts.note: Solomon was a king of Israel

indicators.note: spilled means knocked over and scattered, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word, with its s

explanation.surface: Lily has knocked over the monarch's beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' turns ALES into SEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon's seal is a woodland plant once placed in the lily family.

clue.text: Fruit has corn scattered round it

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the following word
scattered tells us the letters of corn are strewn into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some fruit lies amid a spill of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' makes CRON from CORN, and 'round' puts it around IT: C-IT-RON.
explanation.definitionFit: A citron is a large lemon-like citrus fruit with a thick rind.

clue.text: Girl has an inclination to become a chronicler

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an gives the single letter A, the indefinite article
a list is a ship's lean or tilt to one side

explanation.surface: A young woman is keen to become a historian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' looks like desire, but it is a ship's LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, year-by-year records of events.

clue.text: Someone giving away footwear?.

explanation.surface: An informant hands over some shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints the last letter as D, but it crosses no other light and neither sense fits SNEAKED.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sneaks tells tales on others, and a rubber-soled sports shoe is also called this.

clue.text: Thought marine entered ship with weapons

indicators.note: entered says these pieces go inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
an idea is a thought
RM is the Royal Marines, so a marine

explanation.surface: A notion that a soldier boarded an armed vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEA and RM go inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are weapons carried at the side, such as pistols or swords.

clue.text: Space traveller carries back cat and other animals

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Mars is a planet, a body travelling through space

indicators.note: back says the word for cat is read in reverse order

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An astronaut brings home a cat along with some other creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TOM into MOT, which 'carries' puts inside MARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmots are burrowing rodents of the squirrel family, animals other than the cat.

clue.text: Anglican hymn tune in royal service?

definitions.text: Anglican hymn tune in royal service?

parts.words: Anglican hymn tune in royal service?
parts.note: a tune for a hymn of the Church of England is an air for C of E; and the royal service is the RAF

explanation.surface: A Church of England melody heard at a royal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England: an Anglican tune is an 'air for CE'. The Royal Air Force is the 'royal service'.
explanation.definitionFit: The RAF is Britain's royal aerial fighting service.

clue.text: Drawing in pamphlet upset no-one

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: no gives NO and one gives I

explanation.surface: A picture in a booklet offended nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NO plus I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the act of pulling or drawing a load.

clue.text: Fish, the old party man, is without money

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the party man goes around the money

parts.note: a Whig was a member of the old British party that preceded the Liberals
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: An old-time politician is penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: WHIG goes around TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiting is a sea fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Bad in food, and very bad altogether

indicators.note: in says the first word's synonym goes inside the food word

parts.note: a dish is food prepared for a meal
evil means bad, wicked

explanation.surface: Something nasty in the food makes the whole thing awful.
explanation.walkthrough: EVIL goes inside DISH: D-EVIL-ISH. 'altogether' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish means fiendish, extremely wicked or awful.

clue.text: Means to have business in mine product

parts.note: taken as written
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
mine belongs to me, giving ME

explanation.surface: A way to get into the mining industry.
explanation.walkthrough: CO, the company abbreviation, sits between IN and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's means are their money or earnings.

clue.text: Railwaymen back method used in airport

indicators.note: back says the union's initials are read in reverse

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: Rail workers go back to a technique used at an aerodrome.
explanation.walkthrough: NUR is the National Union of Railwaymen, once a big British trade union; 'back' makes it RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip on which aircraft take off and land, part of every airfield.

clue.text: Changes brought about many disputes

indicators.note: about means around, so the changes word is brought around the next letter

parts.note: alterations are changes
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Alterations led to lots of rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' reads as 'caused', but 'about' puts ALTERATIONS around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Altercations are noisy quarrels or arguments.

clue.text: Act 5 for instance follows terrible opening

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word

parts.note: 5 down is a Russian tea vessel, an example of an urn

explanation.surface: The fifth act comes after a dreadful start.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' points to 5 down: a samovar is an urn. It follows T, the opening of 'terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety act is a performer's spot, as in 'next on the bill'.

clue.text: Not a fellow American, this boy

indicators.note: not says the following letters are excluded from the nationality word

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: This lad is not some guy from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and then M, A, N, in that order, from AMERICAN to leave a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a boy's name, so 'this boy' points to a forename.

clue.text: Shot one of the Innocents Abroad, perhaps?

definitions.text: Shot one of the Innocents Abroad, perhaps?

parts.words: Shot one of the Innocents Abroad, perhaps?
parts.note: The Innocents Abroad is a travel book by Mark Twain, so a figure in it could be called a man belonging to Mark; the clue also wants a good shot

explanation.surface: A crack shot is one of a group of naive tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: The Innocents Abroad is Mark Twain's account of travellers in Europe: its characters are Mark's men.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack shot with a gun is a person skilled at hitting targets.

clue.text: Sprites pestering poor Mrs Elgin

indicators.note: poor implies the lady's name is in a bad way, its letters broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Mischievous imps keep tormenting an unhappy Mrs Elgin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges MRS ELGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gremlins are imaginary mischievous creatures blamed for mechanical faults, a kind of sprite.
